captions.twitter:
One light-year is not “a little farther than the Sun.”

Using IAU definitions: about 63,241 astronomical units fit in one light-year.

Distance math — not a star map.
captions.instagram:
1 AU = 149,597,870.7 km. One light-year ≈ 9.461×10¹² km. Divide them and you get ≈ 63,241 AU.

Sources: IAU AU and light-year definitions
#spacefacts #scale #astronomy
captions.tiktok: A light-year holds about 63,241 Earth–Sun distances (AUs). IAU definitions, not vibes. #space #math #scale

captions.twitter:
An Olympic pool is about 2,500 m³.
Lake Superior is about 12,100 km³.

That is roughly 4.8 billion pools — a volume comparison, not packing.
captions.instagram:
50×25×2 m ≈ 2,500 m³. Lake Superior ≈ 12,100 km³ ≈ 1.21×10¹³ m³. Divide: ≈ 4.84 billion Olympic pools.

Sources: FINA-class pool geometry; EPA/NOAA Great Lakes volumes
#geography #scale #dataviz
